transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mr. Mbeki. Thank you for coming back in to see us today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Morning. I'm glad to be here, but I've got to be back at the shop by two.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I have something important to discuss with you regarding your son's medication from last week. I've discovered that he was given the wrong dosing syringe.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wrong syringe? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The liquid antibiotic itself was the correct strength, but the plastic syringe used to measure the dose was calibrated for a different concentration. Because of that, your son received double the intended dose of the medication for three days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Double? Are you telling me he's been overdosing for three days?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is correct. He received twice the amount we wanted him to have. Does that make sense, or can I explain that in a different way?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense. I just... I did exactly what the pharmacy told me. I used the tool they gave me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you did. This was a mistake made by our team in the dispensing process. I am very sorry. We are responsible for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care whose fault it is right now. Is my son okay? Did you do something to his kidneys or his liver?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how worrying this is. This is a very difficult moment for us to have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's more than worrying. He's a baby.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't afford to have him back in the hospital. I'm already struggling with the time I've taken off work this month.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're feeling the pressure of the business and the stress of the time away.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. I can't just stop everything every time a mistake happens here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize that. Just to make sure we are on the same page about the medical side, do you have any other questions about how the dose was doubled?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No. The "how" doesn't matter. I want to know if he's poisoned.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Based on the specific antibiotic and the dose he received, we do not expect any long-term harm. He is not poisoned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How can you be so sure?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm basing that on the toxicity levels for this specific drug, which are quite high before they become dangerous.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just don't know if I trust the dosing now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that trust has been shaken.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It has. My son is the priority.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He is.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens now? How do we fix this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does "keep an eye on things" mean? Do I bring him back? Do I call someone?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just see how he does over the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. I need to know if I have to miss more work. Do I need to bring him back tomorrow? Next week?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I don't think it's necessary for him to come back immediately. We can just touch base.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Touch base how? Email? Phone?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll probably just send an update or you can call if you notice something.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. You tell me my child took double a drug and then you tell me to "touch base." What specifically am I looking for?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just, you know, anything unusual.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Unusual! He's a baby! He cries! What is "unusual" for this medication?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll let the nurses know to reach out eventually.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure on the timing yet.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have a business to run. I can't be waiting on a "maybe" phone call.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a real plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just continue the correct dose now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the safety of it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It should be fine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're not giving me anything to hold onto here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Frustrating isn't the word. It's irresponsible.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I agree that the error was irresponsible.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If I leave here now, what is the one thing I am supposed to do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just keep giving the medicine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: With the right syringe this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, the one we've provided today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm going to head back to my shop. I hope I don't have to come back here because of another "mix-up."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, remains regulated under significant pushback, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once ('Does that make sense...'), but not twice.

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language, explicitly stated 'We are responsible for this error,' and maintained accountability throughout the encounter.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions ('worrying', 'pressure', 'stress') and referenced the patient's specific situation regarding his business and the baby.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders and vague responses ('keep an eye on things', 'touch base', 'eventually') without specific timelines or a concrete plan.
